findings.reason: the window must be anchored to when the run first reads terminal (its `running → scoring` transition) or to the stall bound, not to the exit instant, or part 2 fixes nothing for the cross-host case and the coordinator's blocking duty merely returns 15 minutes later.
findings.text: §33's part 2 anchors the non-blocking `review-queued` window to the worker's exit ("Once the worker has exited, its review duty reads as review-queued ... for one reflex sweep"; the fixture is "a run whose worker exited less than one reflex sweep ago"), but part 1 makes a cross-host run read `running` until its stream is quiet past `LOG_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` (`reckon/crew/node.py:50`, 900 s) because `process_gone` for an unknown liveness consults `_newest_stream_in_motion` (`reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:422`), and the reflex's sweep is `DEFAULT_SWEEP_SECONDS` (120 s, `reckon/crew/resumption.py:412`). By the time such a run first reads `scoring`, its worker exited roughly 900 s ago — far beyond one sweep — so the duty reads `review-missing` at once and the review-queued arm is unreachable for the very population §33 names (both of its runs ran on clu-2002 against a producer on clu-2018).

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py`, `reckon/crew/obligations.py`, `REVIEW_QUEUED_DUTY_KIND` and each cited plan and evidence page resolve (extensionless hrefs read as `<path>.html`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §33 declares a measurable done-when with a declared negative control (reverting `deferred_outcome` to `alive is True` must turn the first case red), and its part-2 assertion fails on the unfixed tree because the duty today reads `review-missing`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative-control log is written under the run directory, the durable path the plan's other sections use.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §33 introduces no symbol, comment or filename carrying a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the two parts' timing windows do not overlap for the cross-host run §33 exists for, so the `review-queued` arm never fires there.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §33 carries one goal, that a delivered run owes no review before the reflex has had its turn, realised as two coupled readings of one classification.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every depends-on in `plan-section-depends-on` resolves to a section that exists, and §33's cross-plan serialization on `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` with seat §14 is recorded in followup `f-tmstwiw-031-033`, which also carries §33's one-line invocation.
